page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 5760 GB local NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong processing capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is particularly notable; uncached read-only and write large-block memory bandwidth tests place this server in the top 10% tier, reaching 467.73 GB/sec and 282.99 GB/sec respectively. However, other operations such as PassMark database operations, Redis SET performance at 51.19 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 20.63 GB/sec align with average mid-tier expectations.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and the substantial 5760 GB local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound and storage-intensive workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without noisy-neighbor interference, though the 2.0 GHz clock speed represents a tradeoff compared to higher-frequency compute-optimized instances. This profile is highly suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise applications requiring significant local storage capacity.
